rapport_notes: Brianne is warm, conversational, uses humor ('35 feet is like a school bus'), and matches the customer's energy naturally throughout.
process_discipline_notes: Rep asked 'do you have any questions for me?' at the end but did not hold silence—she jumped back in immediately with the bed reassembly answer before the customer could respond.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep launches directly into perks/differentiators without any framing trade (e.g., 'let me ask you six quick questions, should take five minutes, and then we'll get you an accurate quote'). Opens with: 'And then once we go over all this information I'll send you an email...' then immediately launches into damage coverage, Meet Your Mover, and On-Time Guarantee.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after logistics probing had already started. Rep says: 'and then do you have any specific questions or concerns you want answered on this call. In regards to this move.' This comes after unit number, floor, elevator access, truck-to-elevator distance, and other property details had already been explored.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer says 'I don't think so' in response to the agenda question, and rep accepts this with 'Okay, great' and moves to logistics. No follow-up attempt ('what else might come up,' 'anything about the timeline,' etc.). No concerns were raised, so by the rubric's N/A clause for item #3, this scores as N/A/full credit—but the lack of probing depth when the customer said 'I don't think so' (vs. raising items) means there was genuinely nothing to dig into.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: Covered in Stage 1, unprompted, as part of the opening perk delivery: 'We have a new worries, damage coverage which is our free evaluation coverage included in our hourly rate provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages.'
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Covered in Stage 1, unprompted, as part of the opening perk delivery: 'Then we have our meet your mover feature. A few days before you move, you'll receive a meet your mover email introducing them to you helping ease detention of strangers arriving at your front door.'
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Covered in Stage 1 as part of opening perks: 'and then finally we do have our on time guarantee we value your time. So, if you can't make it in the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.'
evidence_quotes.communication: Never mentioned anywhere in the call. Rep does not cover day-before call, named crew lead, inbox updates, or any communication cadence.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial. Rep gives a range: 'I actually think it would take between four and five hours' and personalizes lightly ('Obviously you only have you only pay for as long as you have us we just like to estimate a buffer'). However, the anchor is weak—no reference to a 'typical [size]' move or clear baseline (e.g., 'a typical 760 sq ft apartment on the 4th floor with elevator usually takes X'). The range is given after the system estimate is mentioned.
evidence_quotes.estimate_is_a_window: Covered: 'and then obviously there are number of factors involved in determining move time but the most important one is how well prepared you are when you get there... the more you do that the more the last time we take and the more efficiency we have so less money or less time you take less money you end up spending.'
evidence_quotes.self_prep_tip: Covered: 'the more you do that [prep] the more the last time we take and the more efficiency we have so less money or less time you take less money you end up spending at the end of the day' — direct tip that customer prep = lower bill.
evidence_quotes.does_that_feel_fair: Not asked. Rep moves to 'do you have any questions for me?' but never uses the 'does that feel fair?' closing language from Sheet 5.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock: Never mentioned. No language like 'your rate locks when you book.'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: No explicit close ask. Call ends with 'I'm gonna send this email over to you right now and then if you do have any questions don't hesitate to reach out' — transactional handoff, not a direct 'would you like our help with your move?' or equivalent close.

top_strength: Brianne nailed logistics discovery—she was systematic, personable, asked clarifying follow-ups (bed frame type, TV size, couch details), and kept the customer comfortable and engaged throughout the diagnostic phase.
coaching_note: Lead with the quid pro quo trade (time-boxed ask + accurate quote promise) before diving into perks or probing, and ask the customer's agenda *before* logistics—these front-load trust and control; also, always deliver the Communication differentiator (day-before crew lead call, inbox updates) and close with an explicit ask ('would you like our help with your move?') plus rate-lock language to lock the sale.
